clue.text: The Spanish invested in second-rate capital

indicators.note: to be invested in something is to be clothed inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: B-grade is second-rate quality
el is the Spanish word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A Spanish group has put money into some inferior capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in' reads as finance but means clothed in, placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Belgrade is the capital city of Serbia.

clue.text: Responsible for what's inside fuse

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to fuse is to bind together
eh? is a way of saying what?; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Someone asks who is to blame for the wiring within a fuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fuse' looks like the electrical part but is the verb, to join.
explanation.definitionFit: To be behind a scheme is to be the cause of it, responsible for it.

clue.text: Make ungainly progress, turning two lengths in lido

indicators.note: the pair of letters goes inside the reversed word
turning around makes the letters run the other way

parts.note: a lido is an open-air swimming pool
L is short for length, so two of them

explanation.surface: A clumsy swimmer turning after two lengths of the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' applies to the lido, not the lengths; 'in' places the lengths inside the turned pool.
explanation.definitionFit: To lollop is to move in a loping, awkward, bounding way.

clue.text: Choice role void — US entertainer almost beside herself!

indicators.note: the shortened entertainer stands next to the other piece
a void word is empty, so only its outer letters remain

parts.note: Cher is known by the one name, so she is herself

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Cher is an American singer and actress

explanation.surface: A fussy part for an American star who is nearly hysterical.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is 'role' emptied; CHER appears twice, the second missing its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Recherché describes something rare and choice, carefully sought out.

clue.text: Dieter who won't set off until the very last minute?

indicators.note: set off can mean detonated or launched, so the words before are blown into a new order

explanation.surface: A slimmer who procrastinates before heading out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set off' looks like leaving on a journey but signals that 'Dieter who won't' is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from horse racing, where the finish was marked by a wire; it means the last possible moment.

clue.text: Borne by lymph, a sickness occurring in stages

indicators.note: the letters are carried within the words that follow, spanning the run of text

explanation.surface: An illness carried in the lymphatic system that comes and goes in phases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Borne by' signals the answer is carried inside 'lymph, a sickness', spanning the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: Phasic is the adjective meaning happening in distinct phases or stages.

clue.text: Moveable part in breathing equipment

indicators.note: the letters lie in the words that follow, spanning the gap

explanation.surface: A component that shifts in a respirator or diving apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinge is the jointed fitting on which a door or lid swings.

clue.text: Insubstantial small muscle, one failing in test

parts.note: pec is short for pectoral muscle

indicators.note: a piece failing to be in something is missing from it

parts.note: a trial is a test
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A weak, puny muscle that does not pass the examination.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectral means ghostly, without bodily substance.

clue.text: Tackle Tory cover-up

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the Tory party
a front is a facade that hides what is behind it

explanation.surface: Taking on a Conservative political scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: To confront a problem is to face and deal with it, to tackle it.

clue.text: When speaking comprehensively, subdue expletive

indicators.note: the word is to be heard rather than read, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: wholly means comprehensively, completely
to cow someone is to subdue them by intimidation

explanation.surface: Someone talking at length about overpowering others, then swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When speaking' applies only to WHOLLY, which said aloud matches HOLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy cow is an exclamation of surprise, a mild oath.

clue.text: Light note introduced to night-time service

indicators.note: one piece is put into another, so the letter goes inside the word for late hours

parts.note: late can mean in the night, as in a late show
RN, the Royal Navy, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A musical note is added to an evening church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' looks like a church service but is the Royal Navy, RN; N goes into LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp, a source of light.

clue.text: Premier team cracked it secretly, pocketing diamonds

indicators.note: pocketing something takes it inside, so the gems go within
cracked means broken up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A top side broke into somewhere quietly and stole diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked' looks like a safe-breaker's verb but signals the anagram; the Premier League is England's top football division.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicester City play football in the Premier League, England's top division.

clue.text: Weeping mother returned popular award

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A tearful mother gives back an honour from the public.
explanation.walkthrough: Only IN is read backwards; OBE is a British honour awarded by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Niobe wept endlessly for her slain children and was turned to stone.

clue.text: Three months guarding border's a tricky problem

indicators.note: to guard is to surround protectively, so the outer word holds the other within

parts.note: a tester is a difficult question or problem
a rim is a border or edge; the 's stands for 'is', a link

explanation.surface: Something about a quarter of a year and a protected frontier that poses a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimester is a period of three months, especially of pregnancy.

clue.text: Relaxing in bar after shower, one can't concentrate

indicators.note: the second part comes after the first in the answer

parts.note: to shower is to scatter, as with confetti

indicators.note: relaxing loosens things, so these letters loosen into a new order

explanation.surface: After a shower, unwinding at the bar, someone finds they cannot focus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' is the verb, giving SCATTER; 'Relaxing' rearranges IN BAR into BRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A scatterbrain is a person unable to focus or think in an organised way.

clue.text: Old slave's link with sultanate

parts.note: a bond is a link or tie
Oman is a sultanate in Arabia

explanation.surface: An ancient enslaved person's connection to an Arabian state.
explanation.definitionFit: A bondwoman was a female slave or serf, an archaic term.

clue.text: Choir with its quavers breaking new ground

indicators.note: to quaver is to tremble, so these letters shake into a new order

explanation.surface: A choir singing its notes in a groundbreaking performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quavers' looks like musical notes but is a verb meaning trembles.
explanation.definitionFit: Something historic is momentous, a milestone that breaks new ground.

clue.text: Sellers turned up bearing dressing material for minor wound

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so one piece carries the other inside
in a down answer, turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: reps are sales representatives
lint is a soft fabric used for dressing wounds

explanation.surface: Salespeople arrive carrying bandages for a small cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' suits a down answer, read upwards; 'bearing' means carrying inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A splinter of wood lodged in the skin makes a tiny injury.

clue.text: Executing rogue, sorrowful earl replaces head of axe

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous rogue

indicators.note: one letter takes another's place in the word for grieving

parts.note: lamenting means mourning, sorrowful

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A grim scene of beheading a villain, with a grieving nobleman taking over the axe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Executing' suggests the gallows but means carrying out; the earl's letter replaces the axe's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Implementing a plan means carrying it out, executing it.

clue.text: Fruit — it's wrapped in rind for the most part

indicators.note: something wrapped in another sits inside it
most of the word is used, the last letter dropped

parts.note: a crust is a hard outer layer or rind
it, taken as written; the 's is is, a link

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit mostly enclosed by its peel.
explanation.definitionFit: Citrus fruits include oranges, lemons and limes.

clue.text: They usually hold up tails

definitions.meaning: the slender stems that support leaves, flowers or fruit
to tail is to follow secretly, to shadow or pursue

explanation.surface: Something that typically supports the tails of animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Plant stems support blooms, and a stalker follows someone as a tail does.

clue.text: River running through this stratum is increasingly dry

indicators.note: a river running through something passes into its middle

parts.note: a tier is a layer or stratum

explanation.surface: A geological layer with a river flowing through that gets ever more parched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' in the clue is taken literally as the word to be entered into.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirstier is the comparative of thirsty, so more dry or parched.

clue.text: Third of Austrians are obliged to use plane

indicators.note: the third letter of the word is the one taken

parts.note: have to means must, be obliged to

explanation.surface: A third of Austrian people must fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' suggests flying; it is the woodworking tool.
explanation.definitionFit: To shave wood is to smooth it with a plane, removing thin slices.

clue.text: Game first introduced by married couple?

indicators.note: a thing introduced by another comes after it, so the couple come first

parts.note: W and H stand for wife and husband
1ST is the shorthand for first, read as IST

explanation.surface: A game first brought in by a husband and wife.
explanation.walkthrough: W and H are wife and husband; 1ST is read with the numeral as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Whist is a card game for two pairs of partners.

clue.text: Drivers collectively cutting speed in hectic competition

indicators.note: the group cuts into the other word, sitting inside it

parts.note: rate means speed, as in rate of travel
the RAC, Royal Automobile Club, is a British motoring organisation of drivers

explanation.surface: Motorists as a body slowing down in a frantic contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Automobile Club is a British motoring organisation, a body of drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is a fiercely competitive struggle, especially for success at work.

clue.text: Sinful convert ultimately abandons old god

indicators.note: to abandon is to leave behind, so a letter drops out

parts.note: an immortal is a god of ancient myth

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A wicked convert who in the end gives up an ancient deity.
explanation.walkthrough: The T ending 'convert' leaves IMMORTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Immoral means contrary to moral standards, wicked or sinful.

clue.text: Detectives reported on my little grey cells, perhaps

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece written on another follows it

parts.note: cor and my are both exclamations of surprise

indicators.note: reported means as spoken, so the sound of the word counts

parts.note: tecs is slang for detectives

explanation.surface: Detectives' reports on the famous brainpower of a fictional sleuth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little grey cells' is Hercule Poirot's phrase for his brain; TECS heard aloud gives TEX.
explanation.definitionFit: The cerebral cortex is the grey matter of the brain, so example of the grey cells.

clue.text: Any wrinkling in lettuce is a result of oxygen deficiency

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit inside the name of the lettuce

parts.note: cos is a type of lettuce

indicators.note: wrinkling crumples and rearranges, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Crinkly lettuce leaves are explained as a plant short of oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrinkling' shuffles 'Any'; 'in' places the result inside the lettuce.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyanosis is a bluish skin discolouration caused by too little oxygen in the blood.
